NONE: › written abbreviation for
arrive  or
› written abbreviation for arranged by: used before the name of the person who has arranged a piece of music

example: arrival : used in timetables to show the time at which a bus, train, or aircraft reaches a place

NONE: › to formally accuse someone in a law court of a particular crime and ask that person to say if they are guilty or not
提審；提訊；控告

example: He was arraigned on charges of aiding and abetting terrorists.
他被控夥同恐怖分子作案，所以被提審。

I or T: B1 [ I or T ] to plan, prepare for, or organize something

T: B2 [ T ] to put a group of objects in a particular order
整理，使有條理；排列；佈置
› [ T ] to make changes to a piece of music so that it can be played in a different way, for example by a particular instrument

example: I'm trying to arrange my work so that I can have a couple of days off next week.
我正設法把工作安排好，以便下週能夠休息兩天。
The meeting has been arranged for Wednesday.
會議已經安排在週三了。
[ + to infinitive ] They arranged to have dinner the following month.
他們約好在下個月共進晚餐。
I've already arranged with him to meet at the cinema.
我已和他約好了在電影院見面。
She's arranged for her son to have swimming lessons.
她已經安排她兒子去上游泳課了。
[ + that ] I'd deliberately arranged that they should arrive at the same time.
我特意安排好讓他們同時到達。
[ + question word ] We haven't yet arranged when to meet.
我們還沒有約好甚麼時候會面。
She arranged her birthday cards along the shelf.
她把生日卡在架子上擺成一排。
Who arranged these flowers so beautifully?
這些花插得真漂亮，誰的手藝？
His books are neatly arranged in alphabetical order.
他的書都按照字母順序排列得整整齊齊。
Beethoven's fifth symphony has been arranged for the piano.
貝多芬的第五號交響曲被改編成了鋼琴曲。

NONE: › a marriage in which the parents choose who their son or daughter will marry
包辦婚姻

C usually plural: B1 [ C usually plural ] a plan for how something will happen
C or U: B2 [ C or U ] an agreement between two people or groups about how something happens or will happen

C: B2 [ C ] a group of objects that have been put in a particular order or position
› [ C ] a piece of music that has had changes made to it so that it can be played in a different way, especially by different instruments

example: They'd made all the arrangements for the party.
他們為聚會作好了一切準備。
[ + to infinitive ] Arrangements were made to move the prisoners to another jail.
已經作出安排將犯人轉至另一監獄。
What are your current childcare arrangements?
目前你的孩子怎麼照顧？
[ + that ] We had an arrangement that he would clean the house and I would cook.
我們定好了，他打掃清潔，我做飯。
I'm sure we can come to an arrangement (= reach an agreement).
我確信我們之間可以達成協議。
You can only withdraw money from this account by (prior) arrangement (= after making plans to do so) with the bank.
你必須和銀行（預先）約定，才能從這個帳戶取錢。
There was a striking arrangement of dried flowers on the table.
桌上乾花的插花樣式非常引人注目。
This new arrangement of the piece is for saxophone and piano.
這首新改編的樂曲是供薩克斯風和鋼琴演奏的。

NONE: › used to say how bad something is
一派胡言

example: He dismissed the rumours as `arrant nonsense'.
他把那些傳聞斥為「一派胡言」。

NONE: › a large group of things or people, especially one that is attractive or causes admiration or has been positioned in a particular way
（尤指非常有吸引力、令人讚賞並常以特定的方式排列的）一系列，一批，大量，大群
› to arrange a group of things in a particular way
佈置；排列
› to arrange a group of soldiers in a position for fighting
配置（兵力）

example: There was a splendid array of food on the table.
滿桌子都是美味佳餚。
They sat before an array of microphones and cameras.
他們坐在那裡，面對著無數的麥克風和攝影機鏡頭。
A large number of magazines were arrayed on the stand.
報攤上擺放著很多雜誌。
Arrayed (= standing in a group) before him were 40 schoolchildren in purple and green.
40名身穿紫綠兩色校服的小學生列隊站在他面前。

NONE: › dressed in a particular way, especially in beautiful clothes
身穿…服裝的；（尤指）盛裝的

example: She was arrayed in purple velvet.
她身穿紫色天鵝絨禮服。

NONE: › money that is owed and should already have been paid
應付的欠款；逾期的債款

example: rent arrears
逾期未付的租金

T: B1 If the police arrest someone, they take them away to ask them about a crime that they might have committed.
› formal to stop or interrupt the development of something
› formal to attract or catch someone's attention

NONE: B2 the act of arresting someone
逮捕；拘捕

example: He was arrested when customs officers found drugs in his bag.
海關人員在他的手提包裡發現了毒品，把他拘捕了。
The police arrested her for drinking and driving.
她因酒後駕車被警方拘捕。
The treatment has so far done little to arrest the spread of the cancer.
這種療法到目前為止幾乎沒有抑制癌細胞的擴散。
A photo of a small boy arrested my attention.
一張小男孩的照片引起了我的注意。
Two arrests were made, but the men were later released without charge.
有兩人被捕，但後來他們沒被起訴就獲釋了。
She was stopped outside the shop and placed/put under arrest.
她在商店外被截獲逮捕。

NONE: › An arrestable offence is one for which someone can be arrested.
可逮捕的；可拘捕的

example: Not having your license with you while driving is an arrestable offence in many countries.
在很多國家，駕駛時不帶駕駛執照是可導致被逮捕的行為。

NONE: › very attractive in a way that attracts a lot of attention
引人注意的；醒目的；有吸引力的

example: an arresting-looking woman
相貌迷人的女人

NONE: › a substance that reacts with water to release atoms of hydrogen that have a positive electrical charge
阿倫尼烏斯酸，阿列紐斯酸
› a substance that reacts with water to release atoms of a hydroxide
阿倫尼烏斯鹽基，阿列紐斯鹽基
› a medical condition in which the heart does not beat with a regular rhythm, or at the normal rate
心律不齊，心律失常

example: An arrhythmia is a problem with the rate or rhythm of your heartbeat. the management of heart arrhythmia
針對心率不整採取的措施

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] the fact of arriving somewhere

C: › [ C ] informal a baby that has recently been born

example: Hundreds gathered to await the boxer's arrival at the airport.
數百人聚集在機場等候拳擊手的到來。
On arrival at the police station, they were taken to an interview room.
一到警察局，他們就被帶到一間問訊室。

新到的人員被安置在難民營中。

I: A2 to reach a place, especially at the end of a journey

› to happen or start to exist
› If a baby arrives, it is born.

example: What time will your train arrive?

樹葉開始變黃，是秋天到來的前兆。

NONE: C2 to reach an agreement about something
達成…；作出…；得出…

example: We all argued about it for hours and eventually arrived at a decision.

NONE: › a person who is trying to move into a higher class in society

NONE: B2 a weapon that is like a long, thin stick with a sharp point at one end and often feathers at the other, shot from a bow (= a long, thin piece of wood bent into a curve by a piece of string)

NONE: › the sharp point at the end of an arrow
